outcomes.note: Checked AAP and AACAP official outputs and 2026 news. The AACAP clinical practice guideline (JAACAP 2022; summary updated 2026-08-27) suggests that SSRI medication (except paroxetine), preferably fluoxetine, could be offered: it ranks fluoxetine first but still endorses other SSRIs, which the criterion says does not count. AACAP policy statements issued in 2025-2026 (AI in care, service-intensity instruments, intermediate levels of care, ECT and others) contain nothing on antidepressants. AAP antidepressant guidance names escitalopram, fluoxetine and sertraline as the SSRIs with the strongest evidence and gives no warning against non-fluoxetine drugs; the AAP GLAD-PC endorsement was reaffirmed in June 2025 without such a warning. No document from a pediatric-care society recommending against antidepressants other than fluoxetine for youth depression was found as of 2026-09-13.

Fewer than two qualifying shutdowns as of 2026-09-13. Statement date not shown; the checks cover all of 2026.

outcomes.note: Looked for a US health plan (other than UHC and Cigna) whose policy newly covers TMS for patients under 18 with an effective date after 2026-01-05. Plans that already covered adolescents 15+ before the baseline fail the newly test: Humana (2024-04-25), Aetna (2024), Medi-Cal (2024-08-01), TRICARE West (Nov 2025) and Premera (15+ since 2023-02-03; its 2026 revisions concern accelerated TMS and tapers, not age). Neuronetics 2026 releases announce no adolescent coverage policy. BrainsWay 2026 releases (Premera 2026-01-07, Highmark draft 2026-01-21, South Carolina June 2026) concern accelerated-protocol coverage and do not show a plan that previously excluded under-18s.
